chapters.name: Activities of Daily Living
chapters.summary: Bathing, mouth and denture care, grooming, dressing, eating and fluids, toileting and elimination, and rest, sleep, and comfort.
keyPoints: Dress the weak arm first and undress it last.
Check water temperature before bathing and let the resident feel it.

chapters.name: Infection Control
chapters.summary: Hand hygiene, gloves and other personal protective equipment, standard and transmission-based precautions, clean and dirty items, and handling linens and sharps.
keyPoints: Hand hygiene is the most important way to stop the spread of germs.
Use soap and water when hands are visibly soiled.

chapters.name: Safety and Emergencies
chapters.summary: Fall prevention, call lights and bed height, resident identification, restraint alternatives, fire safety (RACE and PASS), and first response to choking, falls, and other emergencies.
keyPoints: Leave the bed in the low position with the call light within reach.
Fire: Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish.

chapters.name: Positioning, Transfers, and Body Mechanics
chapters.summary: Body mechanics for lifting, basic bed positions, turning and repositioning, transfer belts, wheelchair transfers, and helping a resident walk.
keyPoints: Bend at the knees, keep the back straight, and hold the load close.
Place the wheelchair on the resident's strong side and lock the brakes.

chapters.name: Self-Care, Independence, and Restorative Care
chapters.summary: Promoting independence, range-of-motion exercises, assistive devices such as canes and walkers, bowel and bladder training, and care of prosthetic and orthotic devices.
keyPoints: Let the resident do as much as they safely can.
Stop range-of-motion exercise if the resident has pain.

chapters.name: Vital Signs, Measurements, and Reporting
chapters.summary: Temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure, pain, height and weight, intake and output, and observing and reporting changes to the nurse.
keyPoints: Normal adult resting pulse is about 60 to 100 beats per minute.
Report any sudden change in the resident to the nurse.

chapters.name: Emotional and Mental Health Needs
chapters.summary: Basic human needs, adjusting to life in a facility, anxiety and depression, caring for residents with dementia, responding to difficult behavior, and end-of-life care.
keyPoints: With dementia, stay calm, use short simple sentences, and redirect.
Report signs of depression or talk of self-harm to the nurse.

chapters.name: Spiritual and Cultural Needs
chapters.summary: Respecting religious and cultural practices, food customs, and personal beliefs without judging or imposing your own.
keyPoints: Respect the resident's beliefs even when they differ from yours.
Give privacy for prayer or visits from clergy.

chapters.name: Communication
chapters.summary: Verbal and nonverbal communication, active listening, communicating with residents who have hearing, vision, or speech problems, and reporting and recording.
keyPoints: Face a resident with hearing loss and speak clearly in a normal tone.
Use open-ended questions to get the resident talking.

chapters.name: Resident Rights
chapters.summary: Federal resident rights: dignity, privacy and confidentiality, choices, refusing care, personal possessions, grievances, freedom from abuse and restraints, and reporting abuse.
keyPoints: A resident has the right to refuse care; tell the nurse.
Knock and wait before entering a resident's room.

chapters.name: Legal and Ethical Behavior
chapters.summary: Scope of practice, negligence, abuse and neglect, confidentiality, gifts, honest documentation, and the nurse aide registry.
keyPoints: Never do a task you were not trained for or that is outside your role.
Report suspected abuse right away.

chapters.name: Member of the Health Care Team
chapters.summary: The care team and chain of command, the care plan, accepting and refusing assignments, time management, and in-service training.
keyPoints: The nurse supervises the nurse aide.
Follow the care plan and report what you observe.
